standard.notes: Most U.S. state Firefighter I programs are built on NFPA 1001 JPRs. States may add hours, medical, or local modules. Always verify with the state fire training agency.

title: Firefighter I
description: Complete entry-level structural firefighter qualification pathway: prerequisites, knowledge, practical JPRs, and certification readiness.
audience: Probationary firefighter working toward state/IFSAC/Pro Board seal

estimatedRange.typicalDuration: 4–16 weeks full-time academy or longer part-time/volunteer path

prerequisites.title: Minimum age
prerequisites.detail: Usually 18 (some jurisdictions 17 with restrictions). Confirm local rule.

prerequisites.title: Medical / physical clearance
prerequisites.detail: Department or academy medical evaluation; often includes respiratory clearance for SCBA.

prerequisites.title: Physical ability assessment
prerequisites.detail: CPAT or department-equivalent physical ability test is commonly required for hire or academy entry, not always for the cert itself.

prerequisites.title: Background / affiliation requirements
prerequisites.detail: Some states require membership in an organized fire department or enrollment in an approved program before testing.

corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.title: Hazardous Materials Awareness
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.relationship: commonly required before or with FF I
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.notes: Many systems will not issue FF I without current HazMat Awareness (and often Operations).

corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.title: Hazardous Materials Operations
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.relationship: very commonly required with or immediately after FF I
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.notes: Treat as part of the complete entry package in most career departments.

corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.title: CPR / BLS
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.notes: Often required for academy entry or medical module completion.

corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.title: First Aid / Emergency Medical module or EMT
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.notes: Some states embed basic medical; many departments expect EMT-Basic for career hire.

knowledgeDomains.title: Fire department organization, culture, and safety
topics: Chain of command and company roles

knowledgeDomains.title: Fire behavior and building construction
topics: Building construction types and collapse awareness

jprSkillGroups.title: PPE readiness and donning/doffing
skills: Don structural PPE correctly and within expected time
Doff and prepare PPE for reuse
Perform basic PPE inspection and readiness check

jprSkillGroups.title: SCBA operations
skills: Don and activate SCBA
Perform emergency procedures (e.g., low-air, malfunction awareness)
Control breathing and air management under work
Exit hazardous area while on air

jprSkillGroups.title: Ground ladders
skills: Carry, position, raise, and extend ground ladders
Climb and work from ladders with tools
Assist victims / perform basic ladder rescues as trained
Inspect and maintain ladder readiness

jprSkillGroups.title: Hose, nozzles, and water application
skills: Advance charged and uncharged lines
Couple/uncouple hose and operate nozzles
Produce effective fire streams
Extend and replace hose sections
Load hose and prepare for response

jprSkillGroups.title: Water supply support
skills: Connect to hydrant / establish basic supply
Deploy supply line
Support engine operations as assigned

jprSkillGroups.title: Forcible entry
skills: Force entry through common door/window assemblies using appropriate tools
Select tools for the construction encountered
Work as part of a forcible-entry team

jprSkillGroups.title: Search and rescue
skills: Conduct primary search in structure with limited visibility
Remove victims using appropriate carries/drags
Maintain orientation and team integrity
Recognize and communicate hazards during search

jprSkillGroups.title: Ventilation support
skills: Perform horizontal ventilation
Support vertical ventilation operations as assigned
Recognize ventilation effects on fire behavior

jprSkillGroups.title: Fire control / attack
skills: Attack passenger vehicle fires
Attack exterior Class A fires
Attack interior structure fires as part of a team (as trained/authorized)
Operate hoselines under supervision

jprSkillGroups.title: Overhaul, salvage, and property conservation
skills: Overhaul to find hidden fire
Protect property with salvage covers / water control
Recognize secondary hazards during overhaul

jprSkillGroups.title: Scene support and utilities awareness
skills: Illuminate the scene
Control utilities as trained and ordered
Maintain situational awareness and accountability

jprSkillGroups.title: Communications and emergency procedures
skills: Operate portable radio correctly
Transmit required messages and mayday information
Follow company and department emergency procedures

trainingSequence.title: Confirm eligibility and medical readiness
actions: Verify age and affiliation rules for your state/academy
Complete any required physical ability test

trainingSequence.title: HazMat Awareness (and usually Operations)
actions: Complete Operations if required by state or department

trainingSequence.title: Integrated company evolutions
actions: Live-fire training only where authorized and compliant

trainingSequence.title: Cognitive / written exam preparation
actions: Study fire behavior, construction, PPE/SCBA, ops theory
Practice state or academy written exam format
Review local SOPs that will be tested

trainingSequence.title: Skills testing + written testing
actions: Submit required documentation to state / certifying entity

trainingSequence.title: Certification issuance and seal
actions: Obtain IFSAC and/or Pro Board seal if offered by your entity
Store certificate images and numbers in Career Record

assessment.practical: Pass/fail skill stations mapped to JPRs (state or academy skill sheets)
assessment.written: Typically multiple-choice exam on knowledge objectives
assessment.passingCriteria: Set by state certifying entity or accredited academy (commonly ~70% written; practical pass/fail)
documentationNeeded: Application to state / IFSAC / Pro Board process if separate

stateOverlayGuidance.howToUse: Keep this file as the national baseline. Each state pack should only record differences: extra hours, required medical module, whether HazMat Ops is mandatory, testing entity, reciprocity rules, and official URLs.
alwaysVerifyWith: IFSAC or Pro Board accredited entity in that state

sources.title: NFPA 1001 (Firefighter professional qualifications)
sources.note: Purchase/access via NFPA; do not paste copyrighted JPR text verbatim into public materials.

sources.title: State fire training agency directories (USFA / IFSAC member lists)

disclaimer: This is a structured training roadmap for personal professional development. It is not a substitute for your state certifying agency, academy, or department requirements.
